Greeting About IMK
Greeting

A message from
Sonja Steindl

Sonja Steindl
Intendant, IMK · Initiator of IMK Audition

Dear Young Musicians,

Music has been at the heart of my life for as long as I can remember.

Since moving to Vienna in 1972, I have had the privilege of living in a city where classical music is not only a great tradition, but a living part of everyday life. For the past 33 years, through IMK, I have devoted myself to bringing music to the stage and creating opportunities for artists and audiences to meet.

Over the years, I have encountered many exceptionally gifted young musicians, including scholarship students from the University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna (mdw) and the Kronberg Academy. Their dedication and extraordinary talent have deeply impressed me, but they have also reminded me of something essential: talent needs opportunity.

For a young musician, there is an enormous difference between studying a concerto and performing it with a professional orchestra in an internationally renowned concert hall. Such an experience can become an important step toward a professional career.

I came to believe that those of us who have spent our lives in classical music have a responsibility to create more of these opportunities for the next generation.

This conviction led me to initiate the IMK Audition—our first project dedicated to discovering outstanding young musicians and giving them opportunities to perform with professional orchestras on distinguished international stages.

To every young musician considering applying: believe in the work you have done, have the courage to share your artistry, and give yourself the opportunity to be heard.

I sincerely hope that IMK Audition will open new doors for talented musicians and help the next generation take meaningful steps onto the professional concert stage.

I look forward to hearing your music and seeing where your musical journey will lead you.

Sonja Steindl, Intendant, IMK
Initiator of IMK Audition

About IMK

Since 1992,
bridges through music

1992Founded in Vienna
200+Performances arranged each year

IMK — Verein für Internationale Musik- und Kulturförderung — was founded in Vienna in 1992 and has become one of Europe's most active classical concert organisations, putting international artists on many of the world's great stages.

Today IMK connects and organises approximately 200 performances each year at renowned concert halls across Europe. As a professional classical concert management agency, IMK partners with music universities around the world, including the Kronberg Academy and the mdw – University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna.

Why orchestral opportunities matter

Solo recitals and chamber music concerts are relatively easy to organise. However, for emerging musicians, even many such performances may not be enough to attract wider attention. Orchestral performances are different: they require a professional orchestra, a large concert hall, extensive organisation and significant financial resources. For young musicians, opportunities to perform as soloists with an orchestra are therefore rare.

Even highly talented graduates of prestigious music universities are not automatically given such opportunities. Many turn to international competitions, but even winning a competition may lead to only one orchestral performance, with no guarantee of the next. Recognising this challenge, Ms. Sonja Steindl founded IMK Vienna in 1992 with a clear mission: to create more high-quality and accessible orchestral performance opportunities across Europe.

Schwingungen at the Musikverein

As one of its signature projects, IMK launched the Schwingungen Concert Series at the Musikverein Golden Hall in Vienna in 2006, inviting three to four international orchestras each year. Over the past twenty years, IMK has successfully organised more than 58 concerts at the Golden Hall, with further performances already scheduled through 2028. Through this work IMK has developed unique expertise and extensive know-how in organising orchestral performances at this world-renowned venue.

From music education to the professional stage

Music education should no longer end in the classroom. It must evolve into a system that connects talented young musicians directly to real performance opportunities. Together with its partner universities, IMK is working to make this change a reality — building a bridge from music education to the professional stage. The IMK International Concerto Audition is the next step on that bridge.

Visit schwingungen.at

Application Repertoire Q&A
Application guide

Video audition, open worldwide

The IMK International Concerto Audition is open to pianists, violinists and cellists. Applicants are selected through a video audition. Each applicant must submit an audition video of up to 20 minutes and a completed application form. The audition is evaluated by an international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists.

I

Instruments

Piano · Violin · Cello. One soloist is selected for each instrument to form the trio for Beethoven's Triple Concerto.

II

Submission

An audition video of up to 20 minutes (Google Drive link) and the completed online application form (Jotform), including the €100 audition fee paid via PayPal within the form.

III

Jury

An international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists evaluates all videos. Results are announced in the first week of December 2026.

General Provisions

The IMK International Concerto Audition is an international audition open to musicians of all nationalities. All judging is conducted by online video submission (Google Drive link). English is the official language of the audition.

Instruments & Repertoire

Piano · Violin · Cello. Repertoire requirements for each instrument are set out in detail on the Repertoire tab.

Age

There is no age limit. All applicants are judged by the same artistic standard.

Application

  • Applications are made through the online application form (Jotform) on this website. An application is complete only when the application form has been submitted and payment of the audition fee of €100 (PayPal, at the end of the form) has been confirmed. A submitted form without payment is not considered received; the responsibility for a missed payment lies with the applicant.
  • Once payment has been confirmed, a confirmation e-mail is sent. If you do not receive it, please check your spam folder and then contact us by e-mail.
  • The audition fee is non-refundable, except where the audition is cancelled by the organisers.
  • Write your name in English exactly as it appears in your passport. If the payer’s name differs from the applicant’s (e.g. payment by a parent), write the payer’s (cardholder’s) name at the bottom of the application form.
  • Submitted applications cannot be changed. In the case of duplicate applications, the first application submitted will be evaluated.
  • Applicants who cannot use the online form or PayPal may request a written application form and bank transfer details by e-mail. The same deadline applies; please contact us at least 1–2 weeks before the deadline.
  • Applications close on 30 November 2026, 23:59 CET.

Video Submission

  • The audition video may not exceed 20 minutes. Performance time is measured from the start of the video to the end.
  • The video must be recorded in one continuous, unedited take from beginning to end. Video cuts, combining several takes, and audio correction or editing are not permitted. The only exception: if the recording exceeds 20 minutes, the part after the 20-minute mark may be cut off.
  • The camera must be fixed and may not be moved or zoomed during recording. The applicant’s face and both hands must be clearly visible throughout the video.
  • Video and audio quality must be sufficient for the jury to clearly evaluate the performance. Recording with a smartphone is acceptable; clarity of picture and sound matters more than the equipment.
  • Resolution: Full HD (1920 × 1080). 4K is not required. The video file must not exceed 2 GB in size (MP4 recommended).
  • Only videos recorded on or after 1 January 2026 are accepted. A video of a past performance with orchestra is acceptable if it meets all requirements.
  • The use of AI-generated performances, deepfakes, synthesised audio, or any technology that materially alters the performance is strictly prohibited.
  • The video must be uploaded to Google Drive and shared as a link set to "Anyone with the link can view". Do not delete the link or make it private until the evaluation has been completed. File name: Instrument_LastName_FirstName_Country.mp4
  • Applicants who cannot use Google Drive (e.g. in China) may contact us by e-mail for an alternative method of submission.

Judging

Performances are evaluated comprehensively on musicality, technique, interpretation, expression and overall artistry by an international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists. The decisions of the jury are final. No appeals are accepted.

Selection & Concerts

Three soloists — one pianist, one violinist and one cellist — are selected. The selected musicians perform Beethoven's Triple Concerto in C major, Op. 56 with the North Czech Philharmonic Orchestra under Nayden Todorov at the New Year's Concert in the Dvořák Hall of the Rudolfinum, Prague (3 January 2027). Details of rehearsals are communicated directly to the selected musicians. See the Concerts page for the benefits provided to the selected soloists.

Copyright & Personal Data

Applicants consent to the use of submitted videos and photographs for the promotion of the audition and the concerts. Personal data is used solely for the administration of the audition.

Disqualification

Submission of false information, violation of the video rules, misconduct, copyright infringement or violation of these regulations may result in disqualification without refund of the audition fee.

Agreement

By submitting an application, the applicant is deemed to have read and agreed to all regulations of the IMK International Concerto Audition.

Need help with your application?

If you are unable to complete the online application form, or if the form does not work properly for you, please contact us by e-mail at auditionimk@gmail.com. We will be glad to assist you and, if necessary, accept your application by e-mail.

Repertoire

Audition repertoire

The audition repertoire is the applicant’s free choice — one work of your own choosing (one or more movements from a concerto, or a single-movement concertante work), recorded in one continuous take without editing. The chosen work must not exceed 20 minutes in total.

Duration

  • 20 minutes is the maximum permitted time, not a target time to be filled. A shorter movement is not a disadvantage.
  • Performance time is measured from the start of the video to the end.
  • If the chosen movement or work exceeds 20 minutes, play continuously from the beginning and submit the video only up to the 20-minute mark. Skipping a section or joining different sections together is not permitted.
  • Any movement may be chosen (first, second, third, etc.). Two or more movements may be performed in succession, provided the total time does not exceed 20 minutes; if the 20-minute mark is reached during the next movement, submit only up to that point.
  • Single-movement concertos and concertante works (e.g. Rachmaninoff Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini, Gershwin Rhapsody in Blue, Liszt Totentanz) are permitted.

Cuts

  • The solo part may not be shortened. Omitting a section in the middle of the solo part, or cutting and joining different sections together, is not permitted.
  • Customary cuts or reductions of the orchestral tutti passages are permitted, within the range used in published piano reductions or in general performance practice (e.g. shortening a long orchestral passage in which the soloist rests).

Cadenza

  • If the cadenza falls within the 20 minutes, it must be performed. Skipping the cadenza and joining the following section to what precedes it is not permitted.
  • Any cadenza is acceptable — the composer’s, one by another composer or performer, or the applicant’s own. State the composer of the cadenza in the application form.

Accompaniment & score

  • Accompaniment: piano reduction or orchestra.
  • Playing from memory is not required; the score may be used.
  • Please state the composer, work and movement(s) in the application form exactly as performed.

Piano

Maximum 20 minutes
  • One or more movements from a piano concerto of the applicant’s choice, or a single-movement work for piano and orchestra.
  • Accompaniment: piano reduction (second piano) or orchestra.
  • Cuts to the solo part are not permitted; customary tutti cuts are permitted.

Violin

Maximum 20 minutes
  • One or more movements from a violin concerto of the applicant’s choice, or a single-movement work for violin and orchestra.
  • Accompaniment: piano reduction or orchestra.
  • Cuts to the solo part are not permitted; customary tutti cuts are permitted.

Cello

Maximum 20 minutes
  • One or more movements from a cello concerto of the applicant’s choice, or a single-movement work for cello and orchestra.
  • Accompaniment: piano reduction or orchestra.
  • Cuts to the solo part are not permitted; customary tutti cuts are permitted.
Q&A

Frequently asked questions

Answers to the questions we are asked most often about repertoire, timing, video submission, application and payment. If your question is not answered here, please contact us at auditionimk@gmail.com.

1. Repertoire and performance time

Do I have to perform one movement within 20 minutes, or do I have to choose a movement that is 20 minutes long?
20 minutes is the maximum permitted time, not a target time to be filled. An 8-minute movement and an 18-minute movement are both acceptable, and a shorter performance time is not a disadvantage.

If the movement you have chosen exceeds 20 minutes, play continuously from the beginning of the movement and submit the video only up to the 20-minute mark. Skipping the middle section or joining several sections together is not permitted.
The movement I want to play is slightly longer than 20 minutes. May I shorten part of it?
The solo part may not be shortened. There are two options:
1. Apply the customary cuts to the orchestral tutti passages so that the movement fits within 20 minutes.
2. Play from the beginning of the movement, stop at the 20-minute mark, and submit only up to that point.

In both cases, omitting a section in the middle of the solo part, or cutting and joining different sections together, is not permitted.
How is the performance time measured?
It is measured from the start of the video to the end.
Do I have to play the first movement?
No. You may freely choose any movement — the first, second, third, etc.
May I play two or more movements?
Yes. If the movement you have chosen is shorter than 20 minutes, you may play that movement to the end and then continue with the next movement. However, the total performance time may not exceed 20 minutes. If the 20-minute mark is reached while you are playing the next movement, please submit only up to that point.
Are single-movement concertos or concertante works (e.g. Rachmaninoff Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini, Gershwin Rhapsody in Blue, Liszt Totentanz) allowed?
Yes. If the work exceeds 20 minutes, play from the beginning and submit only up to the 20-minute mark.
Whose cadenza should I play?
Any cadenza is acceptable — the composer’s cadenza, a cadenza by another composer or performer, or a cadenza composed by yourself. Please state the composer of the cadenza you use in the application form.
May I omit the cadenza?
If the cadenza falls within the 20 minutes, it must be performed. Skipping the cadenza and joining the following section to what precedes it is not permitted.
Do I have to play from memory?
No. Playing from memory is not required; you may perform with the score.
How much may be cut when cutting the tutti passages?
Cuts are permitted within the range used in published piano reductions or in general performance practice. A typical example is shortening a long orchestral passage in which the soloist rests. The solo part may not be shortened.

2. Video submission

May I edit the video?
No. The video must be recorded in one continuous, unedited take from beginning to end. Video cuts, combining several takes, and audio correction or editing are all not permitted. The only exception: if the video exceeds 20 minutes, cutting off the part after the 20-minute mark is permitted.
Is there anything I should pay attention to when recording?
The camera must be fixed. The camera may not be moved or zoomed during recording. The applicant’s face and both hands must be visible throughout the video. Sound quality is important for the evaluation, so please check the recording conditions in advance.
Until when must the video have been recorded?
Only videos recorded on or after 1 January 2026 are accepted.
May I record with a smartphone?
Yes. The clarity of the picture and the sound quality matter more than the recording equipment.
How do I submit the video?
Please submit the video as a Google Drive link. Do not delete the link or change it to private until the evaluation has been completed.
May I change the video after submitting?
Submitted applications cannot be changed. In the case of duplicate applications, the first application submitted will be evaluated.

3. Application and payment

When is my application complete?
The application is complete only once payment of the audition fee has been confirmed. Even if you have submitted the application form, it is not considered received if payment has not been made. If an application is not received because payment was missed, the responsibility lies with the applicant. Please make sure to complete the payment after submitting the application form.
How can I check that my application has been received?
Once payment has been confirmed, a confirmation e-mail will be sent. If you have not received the e-mail, please check your spam folder and then contact us by e-mail.
Can the audition fee be refunded?
Once paid, the fee is not refundable, except where the audition is cancelled by the organisers.
How should I write my name on the application form?
Please write your name in English exactly as it appears in your passport. If the name of the payer differs from that of the applicant (e.g. payment by a parent), please write the payer’s (cardholder’s) name separately at the bottom of the application form.

4. If you cannot use the online application form or PayPal (including information for applicants from China)

I cannot access the online application form (Jotform), or payment by PayPal is difficult for me.
Please contact us by e-mail. We will send you a written application form and provide instructions for paying the audition fee by bank transfer. International transfer fees are borne by the applicant. Please be sure to state the applicant’s name when making the transfer.
Google cannot be used in China. How do I submit my video?
Please contact us by e-mail and we will provide an alternative method of submission.
Does the same deadline apply to written applications?
Yes. Both the written application form and the payment of the audition fee must be completed by the same deadline. As the procedure may take some time, please contact us at least 1–2 weeks before the deadline.
How to apply

Three steps to the stage

Prepare your video

Record your audition video (max. 20 minutes) and upload it to Google Drive. Set sharing to "Anyone with the link can view" and copy the link.

Complete the application form

Fill in the online application form (Jotform) with your details, biography, photo and Google Drive link. Write your name exactly as it appears in your passport. The €100 audition fee is paid via PayPal at the end of the form — the application is complete only once payment has been made.

Open application form

Receive your confirmation

Once your payment has been confirmed, you will receive a confirmation e-mail. If it does not arrive, please check your spam folder and then contact us at auditionimk@gmail.com. Submitted applications cannot be changed.

€100Audition fee · non-refundable

The fee is paid via PayPal within the application form. If you are unable to use PayPal, please contact us by e-mail and we will provide bank transfer details (international transfer fees are borne by the applicant).

Before you submit, please check

  • Your video is no longer than 20 minutes, recorded in one continuous take, and the Google Drive link opens without a permission request.
  • Your name on the form matches your passport; if someone else pays, the payer’s name is written at the bottom of the form.
  • You completed the PayPal payment at the end of the form — the application is complete only once payment is confirmed.
  • Your biography (max. 200 words) and a recent photo are ready to upload.
  • You are available in the Czech Republic from late December 2026 to 3 January 2027.

  • Resolution: Full HD (1920 × 1080). 4K is not required. The video file must not exceed 2 GB in size (MP4 recommended).
  • Only videos recorded on or after 1 January 2026 are accepted. A video of a past performance with orchestra is acceptable if it meets all requirements.
  • The use of AI-generated performances, deepfakes, synthesised audio, or any technology that materially alters the performance is strictly prohibited.
  • The video must be uploaded to Google Drive and shared as a link set to "Anyone with the link can view". Do not delete the link or make it private until the evaluation has been completed. File name: Category_LastName_FirstName_Country.mp4
  • Applicants who cannot use Google Drive (e.g. in China) may contact us by e-mail for an alternative method of submission.

Judging

Performances are evaluated comprehensively on musicality, technique, interpretation, expression and overall artistry by an international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists. The decisions of the jury are final. No appeals are accepted.

Selection & Concert

One pianist is selected. The selected soloist performs Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 9 or 10 with the Atlantida Chamber Orchestra under Manuel Tevar at the Víctor Villegas Auditorium, Murcia (14 May 2027). Details of rehearsals are communicated directly to the selected musicians. See the Concerts page for the benefits provided to the selected soloists.

Copyright & Personal Data

Applicants consent to the use of submitted videos and photographs for the promotion of the audition and the concerts. Personal data is used solely for the administration of the audition.

Disqualification

Submission of false information, violation of the video rules, misconduct, copyright infringement or violation of these regulations may result in disqualification without refund of the audition fee.

Agreement

By submitting an application, the applicant is deemed to have read and agreed to all regulations of the IMK International Concerto Audition.

Need help with your application?

If you are unable to complete the online application form, or if the form does not work properly for you, please contact us by e-mail at auditionimk@gmail.com. We will be glad to assist you and, if necessary, accept your application by e-mail.

Repertoire

Audition repertoire

The audition repertoire is the applicant’s free choice — one work of your own choosing, recorded in one continuous take. The chosen work must not exceed 20 minutes in total. (The fixed programme performed by the winners is shown on the Concerts page.)

Duration

  • 20 minutes is the maximum permitted time, not a target time to be filled. A shorter movement is not a disadvantage.
  • Performance time is measured from the start of the video to the end.
  • If the chosen movement or work exceeds 20 minutes, play continuously from the beginning and submit the video only up to the 20-minute mark. Skipping a section or joining different sections together is not permitted.
  • Any movement may be chosen (first, second, third, etc.). Two or more movements may be performed in succession, provided the total time does not exceed 20 minutes; if the 20-minute mark is reached during the next movement, submit only up to that point.
  • Single-movement concertos and concertante works (e.g. Rachmaninoff Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini, Gershwin Rhapsody in Blue, Liszt Totentanz) are permitted.

Cuts

  • The solo part may not be shortened. Omitting a section in the middle of the solo part, or cutting and joining different sections together, is not permitted.
  • Customary cuts or reductions of the orchestral tutti passages are permitted, within the range used in published piano reductions or in general performance practice (e.g. shortening a long orchestral passage in which the soloist rests).

Cadenza

  • If the cadenza falls within the 20 minutes, it must be performed. Skipping the cadenza and joining the following section to what precedes it is not permitted.
  • Any cadenza is acceptable — the composer’s, one by another composer or performer, or the applicant’s own. State the composer of the cadenza in the application form.

Accompaniment & score

  • Accompaniment: piano reduction or orchestra.
  • Playing from memory is not required; the score may be used.
  • Please state the composer, work and movement(s) in the application form exactly as performed.

Piano

Maximum 20 minutes
  • One or more movements from a piano concerto of the applicant’s choice, or a single-movement work for piano and orchestra.
  • Accompaniment: piano reduction (second piano) or orchestra.
  • Cuts to the solo part are not permitted; customary tutti cuts are permitted.

Application guide

Video audition, open worldwide

The IMK International Concerto Audition is open to conductors, violinists and flautists. Applicants are selected through a video audition. Each applicant must submit an audition video of up to 20 minutes and a completed application form. The audition is evaluated by an international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists.

I

Categories

Conducting · Violin · Flute. One winner is selected in each category.

II

Submission

An audition video of up to 20 minutes (Google Drive link) and the completed online application form (Jotform), including the €100 audition fee paid via PayPal within the form.

III

Jury

An international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists evaluates all videos. Results are announced on 15 March 2027.

General Provisions

The IMK International Concerto Audition is an international audition open to musicians of all nationalities. All judging is conducted by online video submission (Google Drive link). English is the official language of the audition.

Categories & Repertoire

Conducting · Violin · Flute. The audition repertoire is the applicant’s free choice; see the Repertoire tab.

Age

There is no age limit. All applicants are judged by the same artistic standard.

Application

  • Applications are made through the online application form (Jotform) on this website. An application is complete only when the application form has been submitted and payment of the audition fee of €100 (PayPal, at the end of the form) has been confirmed. A submitted form without payment is not considered received; the responsibility for a missed payment lies with the applicant.
  • Once payment has been confirmed, a confirmation e-mail is sent. If you do not receive it, please check your spam folder and then contact us by e-mail.
  • The audition fee is non-refundable, except where the audition is cancelled by the organisers.
  • Write your name in English exactly as it appears in your passport. If the payer’s name differs from the applicant’s (e.g. payment by a parent), write the payer’s (cardholder’s) name at the bottom of the application form.
  • Submitted applications cannot be changed. In the case of duplicate applications, the first application submitted will be evaluated.
  • Applicants who cannot use the online form or PayPal may request a written application form and bank transfer details by e-mail. The same deadline applies; please contact us at least 1–2 weeks before the deadline.
  • Applications close on 1 March 2027, 23:59 CET.

Video Submission

  • The audition video may not exceed 20 minutes. Performance time is measured from the start of the video to the end.
  • The video must be recorded in one continuous, unedited take from beginning to end. Video cuts, combining several takes, and audio correction or editing are not permitted. The only exception: if the recording exceeds 20 minutes, the part after the 20-minute mark may be cut off.
  • The camera must be fixed and may not be moved or zoomed during recording. The applicant’s face and both hands must be clearly visible throughout the video.
  • Video and audio quality must be sufficient for the jury to clearly evaluate the performance. Recording with a smartphone is acceptable; clarity of picture and sound matters more than the equipment.
  • Resolution: Full HD (1920 × 1080). 4K is not required. The video file must not exceed 2 GB in size (MP4 recommended).
  • Only videos recorded on or after 1 January 2026 are accepted. A video of a past performance with orchestra is acceptable if it meets all requirements.
  • The use of AI-generated performances, deepfakes, synthesised audio, or any technology that materially alters the performance is strictly prohibited.
  • The video must be uploaded to Google Drive and shared as a link set to "Anyone with the link can view". Do not delete the link or make it private until the evaluation has been completed. File name: Category_LastName_FirstName_Country.mp4
  • Applicants who cannot use Google Drive (e.g. in China) may contact us by e-mail for an alternative method of submission.

Conducting category — video

  • Conductors record themselves conducting a real ensemble (orchestra or instrumental ensemble). The applicant’s full figure and the background must be clearly visible in the frame, filmed facing the camera (from the players’ perspective).
  • The use of a baton is optional.
  • As for all categories, the video is one continuous take and may not exceed 20 minutes.

Judging

Performances are evaluated comprehensively on musicality, technique, interpretation, expression and overall artistry by an international jury of conductors and distinguished instrumentalists. The decisions of the jury are final. No appeals are accepted.

Selection & Concert

One winner is selected in each category. The Conducting winner conducts the Bohuslav Martinů Philharmonic Orchestra, with the Violin and Flute winners as soloists, at the Ehrbar Hall, Vienna (29 May 2027). Details of rehearsals are communicated directly to the selected musicians. See the Concerts page for the benefits provided to the selected soloists.

Copyright & Personal Data

Applicants consent to the use of submitted videos and photographs for the promotion of the audition and the concerts. Personal data is used solely for the administration of the audition.

Disqualification

Submission of false information, violation of the video rules, misconduct, copyright infringement or violation of these regulations may result in disqualification without refund of the audition fee.

Agreement

By submitting an application, the applicant is deemed to have read and agreed to all regulations of the IMK International Concerto Audition.
